front.title: Hereditary Authorization and Runtime-Bound Application Channels: Problem Statement and Requirements

abstract.t:
Existing Internet security mechanisms authenticate communication endpoints, human principals, and software workloads. However, independent implementations do not necessarily share a common representation of the relationship between an originating authorization, subsequent workload generations, delegated permissions, and resulting application effects across administrative boundaries. This document investigates whether additional interoperability conventions are needed to preserve and enforce that relationship.
The proposed model establishes a bounded root of authority through an originating authorization. Descendant workloads operate under independently identifiable, revocable, non-expanding grants. Application exchanges associate requests and responses with their execution principals, authorization lineage, policy context, operation identifiers, and replay-protection state. Protected resources retain final authority over their data and effects.
This document identifies the interoperability problem, trust boundaries, security objectives, and unresolved architectural decisions. It distinguishes requirements for future profiles from behavior described for the experimental review profile http6-rw- review-1.0. It does not establish the necessity of a new transport, select a production cryptographic construction, or claim independently reproduced security or interoperability results.
HTTP6 is a project designation, not an assigned HTTP version, ALPN identifier, URI scheme, or service port.
